task.name: Post-run evidence-backed summaries
task.story_text:
## What

After a completed run, TheForge can emit an optional evidence-backed run summary that captures what changed, what was learned, review insights, and complexity signals in a structured advisory artifact.

## Why

Layer 1 already captures richer run inputs in the audit trail, but future agents still cannot reuse the lessons from completed work. The missing Layer 2 artifact turns a run from raw history into bounded, evidence-backed knowledge that later context assembly can consume.

## Acceptance criteria

- A completed run can produce a structured run-summary artifact keyed by `run_id`.
- Summary generation is optional and non-load-bearing: a summary failure does not change the run outcome.
- Every learned claim in the summary carries at least one concrete evidence reference from the run, such as a finding, plan step, review cycle, file path, or diff reference.
- Summaries with learned claims that have no evidence are rejected rather than persisted.
- The summary records enough structured fields to support later indexing by changed files, domain or story shape, learned patterns, review insights, and complexity signals.
- Summaries are written to the shared knowledge-summary surface described by #787 and remain linked to the authoritative run record.
- A configuration key controls summary generation; when it is set to disabled, no summary agent is invoked and no summary artifact is written.
- Tests cover successful summary persistence, validation failure for unevidenced learned claims, disabled-summary behavior, and non-load-bearing failure behavior.

## Example

After a retry-related story completes, a summary records that retry behavior changed, names the modified files, captures a learned claim about timeout handling, and cites the review finding or plan step that supports the claim. If the summary agent proposes a broad claim without evidence, that claim is omitted or the summary is rejected.

## References

- #787
- `docs/plans/knowledge-capture.md`

handoff.summary: Implemented Layer 2 evidence-backed run summaries. Added a disabled-by-default knowledge.run_summaries config gate (KnowledgeConfig, strict bool validation, generated-config comment, inputs-reference docs). Added src/theforge/knowledge_summary.py as the schema boundary: it extracts a RunAnchors set from the authoritative audit (finding registry ids, plan step ids, review cycles, changed-file paths, diff refs), parses the agent's rooted run_summary: YAML, and rejects any learned claim whose evidence list is missing, empty, or cites a reference that does not resolve against those anchors. Accepted content is merged with mechanically-derived indexing fields (changed files, domains, story shape, review finding views, iteration/cycle/regen/cost signals) so the agent supplies prose and claims while the coordinator supplies every countable fact, then persisted atomically to .forge/knowledge/summaries/{run_id}.yaml with an authoritative_run_record backlink. Prompt construction lives in task/summary_prompts.py; control flow in coordinator/knowledge_summary_flow.py, invoked from cli/shared._write_audit and sprint/audit._write_story_audit after the authoritative record is written. Generation is gated on success + DONE + run_id + config, guarded on artifact existence for exactly-once billing across repeated writer calls, confined to a tool-free API transport (an empty allowlist on a CLI profile grants unrestricted tools), and wrapped so no failure path can raise.

story_deviations: Plan Step 3 specified dispatch via model_ref_to_profile with no tools. The plan reviewer correctly flagged that an empty allowed_tools tuple omits --allowedTools on the Claude CLI and grants its unrestricted default set. Dispatch is therefore restricted to an API transport (derived from plan.ref, or its api_fallback when the plan model is a CLI), where runners.api serves an empty allowlist as a genuinely tool-free stateless call. Consequence worth flagging: a project whose plan model is CLI-only with no transport_fallback configured gets no summaries — generation skips with a warning naming the fix rather than dispatching an unbounded agent.

Plan Step 3 named result.phase.name == 'DONE' plus config as the gate; an artifact-existence check was added on top, because sprint/runner.py calls _write_story_audit several times for the same finished story and each call would otherwise dispatch a billed agent.

The summary schema splits agent-authored from coordinator-authored fields more strictly than the plan doc's example: the agent does not supply files_modified, cycle counts, or costs. This is what makes the indexing fields trustworthy, and it means an agent-proposed file list is discarded rather than merged.
deferred_items: Layer 3 consumption is out of scope. knowledge.prior_run_context is parsed and type-checked so a typo is a config error, but nothing reads it and it is deliberately absent from the generated starter config.

The summary agent's spend lands in no run ledger (the run's cost accounting has closed by then). It is recorded on the artifact as generation.cost_usd so it is visible next to what it paid for, but it is not aggregated anywhere — worth a follow-up if summaries are enabled broadly.

handoff.summary: Iteration 2 is an advisory cleanup pass on an already-APPROVED implementation; the feature itself is unchanged from iteration 1. Fixed the single carried P2: validate_proposed_summary iterated the optional learned_patterns and review_insights fields without checking they were lists, so a scalar YAML value ('learned_patterns: retry-decorator') decomposed into one-character entries and poisoned the very indexes those fields exist to feed. Both fields now go through a shared _string_list() helper that raises SummaryValidationError for a scalar or for a structured (dict/list) entry, while an omitted field still yields an empty list. I swept the rest of the module for the same pattern: what_was_learned and evidence already carried isinstance list guards, and the remaining iteration sites read coordinator-produced audit data with per-entry isinstance(dict) filters, so no other occurrence needed patching. The rejection lands inside the existing SummaryValidationError catch in maybe_generate_run_summary, so the non-load-bearing invariant is unaffected — a malformed summary is warned about and dropped rather than persisted. Iteration 1's implementation (KnowledgeConfig gate, knowledge_summary.py schema boundary with anchor-resolution evidence validation, task/summary_prompts.py, coordinator/knowledge_summary_flow.py wired into cli/shared._write_audit and sprint/audit._write_story_audit) is otherwise untouched.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 carries the plan's stated overclaim risk: it only requires an evidence item to contain an anchor-shaped field. It does not verify that a finding ID, plan-step ID, review cycle, file path, or diff reference actually exists in the supplied audit, so a hallucinated reference such as finding_id f-999 would pass and violate the evidence-from-the-run criterion.
  Suggestion: Build type-specific valid-anchor sets from the authoritative audit and reject references that do not resolve. Add tests for nonempty but unknown finding IDs, step IDs, cycles, paths, and diff references.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3's proposed 'no tools' profile is not feasible through model_ref_to_profile(..., allowed_tools=()). src/theforge/runners/runner_claude.py explicitly documents that an empty allowed_tools tuple omits --allowedTools and grants Claude CLI's unrestricted default tools; model_ref_to_profile also defaults to workspace-write at the project root. The supposedly bounded summary agent could therefore inspect or mutate repository state.
  Suggestion: Use a dispatch path that mechanically enforces a tool-free, non-writing invocation, such as a stateless API profile, or extend the runner/profile contract with an explicit deny-all tool mode and appropriate containment before wiring summary generation.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3 attaches generation to _write_story_audit without an exactly-once seam. src/theforge/sprint/runner.py calls that writer repeatedly for the same successful DONE result during pending integration, landing, queued-PR resolution, and wrap-up, so the summary agent may run multiple times and overwrite the same run_id artifact.
  Suggestion: Make generation idempotent per run_id or invoke it from a single terminal persistence seam after the canonical per-run record is written, and test repeated audit writes for one DONE result.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (carried, non-AC): the plan deliberately declines to add a pointer field on the authoritative audit record, linking only from summary → run. The AC only requires the summary remain 'linked to the authoritative run record', which the authoritative_run_record field satisfies, so this does not block — but the run record itself will carry no discoverable pointer to its summary, which later Layer 3 consumption will have to resolve by path convention.
  Suggestion: Either accept path-convention lookup explicitly (document it in Step 4's doc edit) or add a single optional knowledge_summary_path key to the per-run JSON written by _write_per_run_record in src/theforge/cli/shared.py, which is additive and low blast radius.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] The summary agent dispatched through run_agent spends money after the run's audit/cost accounting has been produced, so its cost lands in no ledger. Given forge's existing cost-unknown checks, an unattributed post-run invocation is an accounting blind spot.
  Suggestion: Log the summary invocation's cost_usd from the AgentResult and record it in the summary artifact (e.g. a generation_cost_usd field) so the spend is at least visible next to the artifact it produced.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Two independent seams call generate_audit_log for a terminal run — cli/shared._write_audit (used by cli/run.py:297 and cli/review.py:122) and sprint/audit._write_story_audit (line 1499, plus the in-flight path at 1636). Step 3 hooks both, so a run reaching both seams would invoke the summary agent twice for the same run_id.
  Suggestion: Make persistence idempotent by skipping generation when .forge/knowledge/summaries/{run_id}.yaml already exists, and skip the in-flight call site at sprint/audit.py:1636.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 adds knowledge.prior_run_context which no step in this plan reads; it is Layer 3 scope.
  Suggestion: Either omit it or keep it undocumented in generate_default_config() so operators are not offered a key that does nothing.

finding_registry.description: When the summary agent emits scalar learned_patterns or review_insights values, the validator persists them as one-character list entries, so learned-pattern and observation indexes contain characters instead of tags or observations.
When forge.yaml sets knowledge to false, config loading accepts the non-mapping value and silently produces disabled knowledge defaults.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
